gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's US store now lists the EB3A as discontinued, even though one ChatGPT answer made the EB3A + 100W kit at $399 its top pick. The kit URL it used now returns HTTP 404. On 2026-11-13 the same store sells the newer Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, 600 W) with a 60 W panel for $399.99, in stock, which is $90 less than the $489.99 Elite 30 V2 + 100 W kit that every chat names.
standout_why: I compared against four pages. OffGridEmpire's under-$500 page (updated 2026-11-12) lists a 'Bluetti EB3A' at $299, does not say whether a panel is included, and does not say the EB3A is discontinued. It lists no Elite 30 V2 kit and no ALLPOWERS kit. PowerSized's kit price guide (updated 2026-10-17) lists only one kit under $600, the Jackery Explorer 300 v2 + 40 W at $419 'from Jackery', but Jackery's own store now says the Explorer 300 v2 is sold out. StormWatts' same-panel-watts comparison (2026-11-08) starts at $699. SolarGenAdvisor's under-$500 page would not load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check it. None of these pages gives a current maker-store price for the Elite 30 V2 + 60 W kit, the Elite 30 mini + 100 W kit, or the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W kit before its code.
decides: The pick stays the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W at $489.99 (BLUETTI US, in stock). The EB3A kit drops out because it is discontinued and its kit page is gone. Our page can offer a cheaper version of the same pick: the identical Elite 30 V2 station with a 60 W panel at $399.99. Within $500, the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W qualifies only with a code: it lists at $531 on ALLPOWERS' US store, and ChatGPT's $477.90 works out to exactly 10% off that. Other notes: the Elite 30 mini + 100 W is now $409.99 (our page says $429.99), and the ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 + 100 W kit (our product) is out of stock at $216.99.
